q: Define the transportation model and solve the MG Auto example.
a: The transportation model determines the shipping schedule minimizing total cost from m sources to n destinations subject to supply and demand. MG Auto: supplies 1000, 1500, 1200; demands 2300, 1400; costs LA 80/215, Detroit 100/108, New Orleans 102/68. Optimal: LA-Denver 1000, Detroit-Denver 1300, Detroit-Miami 200, New Orleans-Miami 1200; cost = 80,000 + 130,000 + 21,600 + 81,600 = \$313,200.

q: How is an unbalanced transportation model balanced?
a: Add a dummy source (if demand exceeds supply) or a dummy destination (if supply exceeds demand) with capacity equal to the difference and zero unit costs. Example: with Detroit capacity 1300 total supply is 3500 vs demand 3700, so a dummy plant of 200 is added; the dummy ships 200 to Miami (Miami is 200 short). A very high cost can prevent shortage at a chosen destination.

q: Explain how production-inventory control is modelled as a transportation problem (Boralis).
a: Sources are production in each month (capacity) and destinations are monthly demands. The unit cost is 40 if produced in the same month, 40 + 0.50 per month of holding if produced earlier, and 40 + 2.00 per month of delay if backordered. With capacities 50, 180, 280, 270 and demands 100, 200, 180, 300 the optimal cost is \$31,455.

q: Summarize the transportation algorithm and the MODI optimality test.
a: Step 1: find a starting basic feasible solution (NW, least cost or Vogel) with m+n-1 basic variables. Step 2: compute ui and vj from ui + vj = cij for basic cells and evaluate ui + vj - cij for nonbasic cells; if all are <= 0 stop, otherwise the largest positive enters. Step 3: use the loop to find the leaving variable and update. For SunRay: NW cost 520, least-cost/Vogel 475, optimal 435.

In a transshipment network goods may pass through intermediate nodes before reaching the destination; nodes with both input and output arcs act as both source and destination. It is converted to a regular transportation model by adding a buffer B (equal to total supply) to the supply and demand of every node, with zero cost for shipping from a node to itself.
